logline: Thirty-three years after losing the All-Valley tournament, down-on-his-luck Johnny Lawrence reopens the Cobra Kai dojo, reigniting his rivalry with Daniel LaRusso and setting off a generation-spanning karate war neither man can walk away from.

renewal.note: Six-season run concluded February 13, 2025 with the final episodes of Season 6. The series began on YouTube Premium in 2018 before moving to Netflix from Season 3 onward.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 50 critics; critics across the board noted the series earned its Karate Kid legacy by taking both leads seriously as flawed men rather than treating the premise as nostalgia exercise.

pull_quotes.text: This marvelous sequel series isn't just a huge suckerpunch of nostalgia for kids of the '80s.
The genius of the series is in having both play believably flawed men who need to turn back to karate.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 launched May 2, 2018 on YouTube Red. The series rehabilitated Johnny Lawrence as a full protagonist with his own moral logic rather than reducing him to a villain turned comic foil. William Zabka and Ralph Macchio play against three decades of assumption, and the show rewards close attention to both. The premise could have been a cheap revival, but the writing is structurally smart: scenes implicate both men as simultaneously right and wrong. The IMDb audience average of 8.72 for the season aligns with the overall momentum around the season.

episode_reviews.title: Ace Degenerate
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere reintroduces Johnny Lawrence in 2018 as a struggling, stubborn man out of step with contemporary life. The decision to open on Johnny rather than Daniel LaRusso announces the show's corrective intent immediately. The episode earns its nostalgic callbacks because they serve character rather than sentiment.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Johnny's first look at the shuttered Valley strip mall where his old dojo stood - the weight of thirty years in one held shot.

critic_note.text: I like the harsh tone and unsparing assessment of misguided men stumbling into something bigger than either of them.

bollymeter.basis: 91% on Rotten Tomatoes from 32 critics; deepens both dojos' philosophies and escalates the generational conflict while the IMDb audience average sits at 8.79, the series' per-season peak.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 aired April 24, 2019, still on YouTube Premium, expanding both the Cobra Kai and Miyagi-do rosters while pushing the rivalry between Johnny and Daniel toward a genuine breaking point. The show deepens the story rather than simply amplifying it. The IMDb audience average of 8.79 across the season is the highest in the entire run. The season’s school brawl finale serves as the operatic set-piece the series had been building toward, delivering on the conflicts it had foreshadowed.
seasons.season_over_season: Expands the dojo rivalry into a full generational war; the school brawl finale delivers on every thread Season 1 planted.

bollymeter.basis: 90% on Rotten Tomatoes from 52 critics; the Netflix debut season brought legacy Karate Kid characters back and sustained the tonal balance between melodrama and genuine feeling.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 marked the show's Netflix debut on January 1, 2021, which expanded its global footprint. A 90-percent Rotten Tomatoes score based on 52 reviews highlights sustained quality, and the season’s standout move was the return of original Karate Kid cast members including Tamlyn Tomita and Yuji Okumoto. The writing handles legacy character reintegration with notable steadiness, grounding flashback material in the series’ ongoing thematic argument about competing versions of mentorship. Johnny and Daniel are drawn into a reluctant alliance, and the season completes emotionally satisfying arcs for both. The IMDb audience average of 8.65 suggests strong acceptance of the Netflix era.
seasons.season_over_season: First Netflix season; Karate Kid legacy cast returns with genuine dramatic purpose rather than fan-service cameos.

bollymeter.basis: 95% on Rotten Tomatoes from 42 critics; Terry Silver's return as principal antagonist gave the season a villain with genuine narrative weight and the All-Valley tournament a satisfying structural payoff.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 launched December 31, 2021, bringing the return of Terry Silver as the season's primary antagonist. The 95-percent Rotten Tomatoes score, based on 42 critics, was the second-highest in the run, with Thomas Ian Griffith's Silver delivering authentic menace rather than pantomime evil. The All-Valley tournament structure gives the season a clean narrative through-line and a climax that resolves multiple seasons of planted conflict. The mix of nostalgia, genuine drama, and the show's characteristic emotional earnestness remains compelling in Season 4. The IMDb average of 8.47 holds above that of most comparable long-run series.
seasons.season_over_season: Terry Silver's comeback gives Season 4 the franchise's strongest villain since the original films, and the All-Valley tournament resolves cleanly.

bollymeter.basis: 98% on Rotten Tomatoes from 48 critics - the series' critical peak; critics and audiences credited the Silver takedown arc and the show's confidence in its own emotionally earnest register.

pull_quotes.text: The show has already surpassed any reasonable expectations, developing a life of its own that proves it wasn't just 'Karate Kid'-ing around.

seasons.review_body: Released September 9, 2022, Season 5 earned 98 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 48 critics as the Silver storyline reached its intended resolution. The season reunited Johnny and Daniel in full partnership against Silver and delivered action sequences that paid off years of training montages. The emotional register, earnest and melodramatic yet unashamed of its feelings, plays as the engine of the show's peculiar power. The IMDb average of 8.56 across the season reflects a viewer base that agreed.
seasons.season_over_season: The Silver arc reaches its peak and resolution, delivering the series' strongest stretch and the most emotionally satisfying installment since Season 2.

bollymeter.basis: 91% on Rotten Tomatoes from 47 critics; a fitting if slightly overstuffed farewell, released in three parts across mid-2024 and early 2025, that earned its goodbyes from most critics.

pull_quotes.text: In unlikely fashion, Cobra Kai wins again.

seasons.review_body: The final season split into three five-episode parts released across July 2024 and concluded February 13, 2025. At 91 percent from 47 critics, the series closed well - the Guardian's verdict was simply 'Cobra Kai wins again.' RogerEbert.com noted that the finale installments were classic Cobra Kai: melodramatic, cheesy, and deeply affectionate toward its characters. The 15-episode count stretched the narrative more than prior seasons warranted, and the three-part release structure meant the ending felt protracted for some viewers. But the show achieved something rare: a six-season run without a collapse in quality, and a finale that respected the characters it had spent years building. IMDb audience average of 8.57 confirmed the ending landed.
seasons.season_over_season: The three-part finale structure runs slightly long, but critics agreed the series closed with integrity intact and all its major character arcs honoured.
